title: Rabbi Zakkai of Alexandria
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:8: he knew how to sweeten the Great Sea, and Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun said, “Had you wished, you could have learned it from him.” In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 7:5: “Rabbi Zakkai, Rabbi Alexandria (Hyman proposes ‘of Alexandria’ and suggests that a dalet became a resh and then separated) mishlach sha’al (Hyman suggests mish’al sha’al, like ba’ei in the Babylonian Talmud): the daughter of an Ammonite convert… Rabbi Yosah (son of Rabbi Bun): Has he not heard what Rabbi Yirmeyah said in the name of the Rabbis and Rabbi Ba?” In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:6: “Rabbi Zakkai of Alexandria asked: A found object,” etc. Hyman infers from this that he belonged to the fifth generation of Palestinian Amoraim, in the time of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun.

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud. The dalet/resh development, mishal reconstruction and generation placement are Hyman’s proposals, not native-pixel or correction-history findings.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:8 includes the sea-sweetening discussion but explicitly calls the relevant knowledge a calculation of water and then a great calculation known to Zakkai of Alexandria. Hyman’s compressed description is retained. His dalet/resh reconstruction, mishal reading and fifth-generation inference remain proposals, not independent evidence of textual history.
